articles.title_orig: Xona Is in Orbit. Its CEO Says U.S. GPS Backup Leans on China.
articles.title_zh: Xona Is in Orbit. Its CEO Says U.S. GPS Backup Leans on China.
articles.content_orig:
By Nick David, Editorial Lead, SatNews
Xona Space Systems put its first six commercial navigation satellites in orbit last week. On Thursday, its CEO laid out why the U.S. needs them: the backup most commercial users rely on today comes from China.
“We actually just launched our first six satellites last week that are going to start providing commercial service early next year,” Xona co-founder and CEO Brian Manning said on the MilSat Symposium panel “GPS Under Attack: Jamming, Spoofing, and the PNT Fight” at Silicon Valley Space Week, moderated by Ahsun Murad of Optimal Satcom. The Pulsar satellites flew Oct. 20 on SpaceX’s Bandwagon-5 rideshare, and Xona has said beta service begins in early 2027. The company closed a $250 million Series D two days after launch.
Manning said the problem is already showing up in drones built by the hundreds of thousands. Drone companies on the military side “are cutting the cable on the GPS chip because they don’t trust it,” he said. “It’s actually worse to have bad location than no location.” Jamming can be worked around with inertial sensors, but bad location “means you’re going to hit your own troops.”
Those builders don’t have access to M-code or other secure signals, Manning said, while faking GPS signals takes about as much skill as “typing the Google.”
Commercial users trying to make positioning more resilient mostly move to multi-constellation receivers, Manning said, and the newest constellation beyond GPS is China’s. U.S. industries from critical infrastructure timing to agriculture to logistics now integrate Chinese signals alongside GPS, “a vulnerability that has been ingrained into pretty much every single aspect of U.S. critical infrastructure,” he said.
Receiver makers can’t simply drop those signals and stay competitive globally, he acknowledged. “But right now relying on Chinese, Russian, et cetera, signals to get resilience does not put the U.S., I don’t think, in a very strong position.”
Col. Jon Strizzi, director of Space Systems Command’s Space Systems Integration Office, gave the Space Force’s GPS update. He said 14 GPS IIIF satellites, the next block, are on contract, with five moving through assembly, integration and test and first deliveries expected in mid-2027.
The panel also included Jeff Janicik, founder and chairman of Innoflight; Monali Jain, founder and CEO of AutonomousLabs.Space; and Sumant Sharma, co-founder and CEO of EraDrive.
Xona’s pitch is that commercial signals from low Earth orbit, roughly 20 times closer to Earth than GPS, can add the precision, power and protection that today’s receivers lack while plugging into the billions of GPS devices already in use.
A storyteller at heart, Nick David covers space policy, satellite markets, defense, and the technologies reshaping how humanity operates beyond Earth. With a background in creative direction, brand strategy, and editorial storytelling, he brings a modern lens to complex subjects and a relentless curiosity about what comes next.
Satnews is a leading provider of satellite news, events, publications, research and other satellite industry information in both commercial and military enterprises worldwide.

articles.title_orig: American chip billionaire Jensen Huang's Nvidia defends his meetings with suspected Chinese spy
articles.title_zh: American chip billionaire Jensen Huang's Nvidia defends his meetings with suspected Chinese spy
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia says billionaire CEO Jensen Huang did nothing unusual in meeting a Chinese executive whom U.S. intelligence officials concluded was gathering information for Beijing.
Nvidia Corp. has defended its billionaire chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, after a report that U.S. intelligence officials concluded a Chinese businesswoman who built a close relationship with him was gathering information for Beijing, and that President Donald Trump was told about it roughly a year ago but did not act.
The woman, Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese national and a former senior executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company that buys Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips and rents out computing power, including to Chinese companies. She has not been charged with any crime, and neither has Megaspeed. U.S. officials did not believe Jensen Huang knew she was collecting information for China, according to people familiar with the classified intelligence. No one has accused him of wrongdoing.
Nvidia said the contacts were routine. "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected," Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo said. "Meetings with customers are part of a C.E.O.'s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." The company said customers such as Megaspeed receive ordinary business information, not trade secrets or anything tied to national security, and that it was confident the government would tell it if it believed someone was a threat to American industry.
Huang, 63, called Nvidia's business with Megaspeed normal on Oct. 29 and said the company had checked how the cloud provider used its chips. "We've studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one," he said. He added that Alice Huang no longer works at Megaspeed.
U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang turned up her contacts with Jensen Huang and led officials to conclude she was passing information to Beijing, according to people familiar with the intelligence. Officials worried she could gain access to sensitive Nvidia technology or insight into Trump's thinking on chip exports to China. The two were photographed together at a bar in Taipei in June 2024 and were seen at a business dinner in May 2025.
Trump was briefed on the findings about a year ago. The administration took no action, and Jensen Huang never received a defensive briefing, the warning U.S. agencies sometimes give Americans who are being targeted by a foreign intelligence service. The White House, the CIA and the National Security Agency declined to comment.
Alice Huang did not respond to requests for comment. Megaspeed said it takes the matter seriously, has hired outside lawyers to run an internal investigation and has told U.S. authorities it will cooperate. China rejected the report. Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called it "baseless and purely slanderous," and the Chinese Embassy in Washington described U.S. accusations as "groundless smears and slanders."
Megaspeed under investigation
The U.S. began looking at Megaspeed in late 2024, when a Commerce Department official visiting its data center in Malaysia found Nvidia equipment still sitting in boxes. Investigators suspected some of its chips were reaching China in breach of U.S. export rules, which bar the sale of Nvidia's most advanced processors there. A Malaysian sister company of Megaspeed bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, according to trade records. Singapore authorities questioned Alice Huang in 2025 and released her.
Senator Tom Cotton asked the Commerce Department in October 2025 to investigate Megaspeed, and the Justice Department took over the case this year. Nvidia said earlier claims that Megaspeed helped Chinese buyers evade U.S. restrictions "were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year." Megaspeed remains a listed Nvidia cloud partner.
The report lands at a sensitive time for Huang, who has become one of Trump's closest business allies. He persuaded the president to allow some chip sales to China in exchange for the U.S. government taking a share of the revenue, and he was a guest at the White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping in September. Trump personally owns Nvidia shares.
Born in Taiwan, Huang moved to the U.S. as a child and co-founded Nvidia in 1993. He has run the company ever since, turning a maker of graphics cards for video games into the dominant supplier of the chips used to build AI systems. His stake in Nvidia has made him one of the richest people in the world.

OpenAI’s latest funding round isn’t quite living up to expectations, according to multiple news reports.
OpenAI was previously reported to be raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation , and then at a $1.25 trillion valuation , ahead of a planned IPO. But The Financial Times reported Friday that the company has subsequently lowered its funding target to $20 billion, with a first close that’s expected to be even lower than that.
The round will be led by a group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, the FT said. A subsequent retail offering for wealthy individuals could bring the total funding amount to the $20 billion target.
A follow-up story in The Wall Street Journal offered more details, namely that the company has secured $11 billion so far, and that its fundraising efforts had met with a “tepid” response from some large investors.
TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment. The company’s reported funding challenges could be blamed, in part, on bad timing, as Wall Street investors have become wary of heavy AI infrastructure spending , leading to a major sell off of tech stocks. And Anthropic’s planned IPO could be facing challenges , too.

articles.title_orig: Tech stock meltdown could get a lot of worse if history is any guide
articles.title_zh: Tech stock meltdown could get a lot of worse if history is any guide
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
And you thought this week has been painful for the tech trade.
If history is any guide, the pain for tech may only be just beginning!
The S&P 500 tech sector has seen six pullbacks of 10% or more since 2023, points out Truist chief markets strategist officer (chart below), including the current one. But four of the six plunges have ranged from 14% to 27%.
"The story is no longer simply about the strength of AI demand. Wall Street is increasingly demanding evidence that heavy investment will translate into durable profits and cash flow," Lerner says.
That's putting it lightly.
The AI trade took a serious beating Friday, with more than $1 trillion in market value wiped away as investors fretted about weakening cash flow profiles of Big Tech as it spends aggressively on AI. The news on the cash front worsened as the weak went along.
Google showed negative free cash flow in the third quarter when it reported mid-week. That was followed by another free cash flow negative call out when Amazon reported Thursday evening.
A week ago, Meta posted negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012.
None of these top tech names suggested their AI spending would be slowing down, quite the contrary.
The Nasdaq 100 went onto tank 3.4% while the broader S&P 500 fell 1.8%.
The S&P 500's tech sector tumbled more than 4.2%.
"The disruption caused by AI is on full display during tech earnings and the uncertainty around which names and sectors will be the disruptors vs the disrupted," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said. "This is not the time to panic and sell all the tech winners and head into the bunker…as painful as this week is the underlying signs from enterprise AI buildouts are actually more validated than a week ago…given what we heard front and center from the hyperscalers combined with last week's Meta and SpaceX ( SPCX ) numbers. That said, tech players raising money via the bond market, equity offerings, ATMs, etc. has put further pressure on the sector and adding to the overhang seen this week."
Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title_orig: Poland's president accuses Tusk of forced takeover of country's top court
articles.title_zh: Poland's president accuses Tusk of forced takeover of country's top court
articles.content_orig:
Prime Minister Donald Tusk addressed Poland’s deepening Constitutional Tribunal crisis in a televised speech on Saturday evening, vowing that the rule of law would prevail over violence as tensions over the country's judiciary reach boiling point.
The dispute over the composition of Poland’s top court has fuelled an open confrontation with President Karol Nawrocki, who attempted to enter the Tribunal building amid a deadlock over the appointment of new judges on Friday night.
Police surrounded the building as the confrontation unfolded live on television, drawing attention to the crisis beyond Poland and into the wider European political debate.
The opposition has accused Tusk’s government of attempting a coup, while the government says it is pushing ahead with long-needed reforms to restore the rule of law after years of PiS interference in the judiciary.
In his address to the nation, Tusk described Friday’s events as “scandalous incidents” and said he hoped such scenes would never be repeated in Poland. He added that restoring calm could not mean accepting lawlessness or violence.
“A democratic state has to be strong and capable of enforcing justice,” he said.
The dispute over Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal dates back to 2015 , when the governing Civic Platform and opposition Law and Justice parties clashed over the appointment of five judges. It has since developed into a wider conflict over judicial independence, the Tribunal’s composition and the authority of its rulings.
Tusk said his government had tried to resolve the crisis, but its proposals were blocked by PiS and the president, further deepening the dispute.
He said the parliamentary majority then waited for the terms of judges appointed under the previous PiS-led government to expire in an effort to avoid a confrontation.
“We waited calmly for new judges to be chosen, until the terms of their predecessors appointed by PiS expired. The Sejm made its choice, the judges took the oath, but the president did not deign to receive that oath,” Tusk said.
The Sejm, Poland’s lower house of parliament, elected the new judges, who took their oaths of office. Nawrocki did not formally receive the oaths, while Tribunal President Bogdan Święczkowski refused to allow the new judges to take up their duties.
Tusk described the newly elected judges as legally appointed and said they had been attacked. He also criticised politicians and activists linked to PiS and the far-right Confederation party over their conduct during the confrontation.
He compared the dispute to a thief stealing an elderly woman’s handbag and then accusing others of violence when they try to recover it.
“In certain matters there can be no compromise,” he said, adding that lawlessness could not be negotiated away.
Physical force, aggression and party interests must not determine who is right in a state governed by the rule of law, he added.
Tusk also said no politician, including the president, had the right to enter a court or tribunal, issue instructions to judges or intimidate them. He was referring to Nawrocki’s visit to the Tribunal building after turning his plane around while travelling to Senegal.
Tusk warned that pro-Russian groups could exploit the political conflict.
He pointed to Russian bots operating online which, in his assessment, were supporting opponents of Poland’s current constitutional order.
He said the Constitutional Tribunal would operate in accordance with the constitution and independently of the executive.
As head of government, Tusk pledged to provide the institution with the security and conditions needed to carry out its duties.
“And I intend to fulfil this task,” he said.
However, the speech offered no concrete agreement with Nawrocki or detailed plan to resolve the dispute.

articles.title_orig: I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could
articles.title_zh: I built an AI Tamagotchi before Meta could
articles.content_orig:
We have Muse Charm at home.
We have Muse Charm at home.
Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta made AI look so stinking cute by giving it a squishy little face — and this holiday season, he wants to sell you a Muse Charm so you can carry your jolly AI helper around like a Tamagotchi.
But I won’t be buying one, because we have Muse Charm at home . It cost just $50, and I’ve decided the learning experience was worth it.
My version doesn’t sport cameras or a 5G cellular radio , but it really talks to Muse and has cute avatars, too! It doubles as a pocket watch and a remote camera viewfinder, and it can (theoretically) control my smart home.
Or at least it can if you inject a lot of extra vibe code.
Weeks ago, I paid $50 to get a 1.75-inch touchscreen computer pendant drop-shipped from China — specifically the Waveshare ESP32-S3 1.75C . Not only does the push-to-talk AI devkit look a lot like the Muse Charm, but it’s officially sanctioned by Meta. It’s one of the company’s first suggestions if you want to build a “Muse Gadget,” a device that uses Meta’s open-source code and tokens to directly connect to its Muse AI cloud.
When the silver metal pocket watch arrived, it felt pretty useless to start. Setup was easy enough — I just plugged it into my PC and pointed Claude at Meta’s GitHub, then paired it to the Muse phone app. But even after I put Meta’s keys on the device, Muse originally thought I was sending it audio clips to transcribe rather than commands. After I cleared that up, Muse’s responses were still slow, and it didn’t answer me out loud. It was hard to tell what it was saying since it only showed a few words onscreen at a time, with no place to read full messages unless I whipped out my phone with its own Muse app.
Meta’s build also only came with a single Jolly avatar that mostly just sat there and looked cute, and it wouldn’t automatically discover smart home gadgets like Amazon Echo or Google Home devices do. (This gadget really didn’t do anything useful after my initial install.) And though Meta AI software engineers Anant Narayanan and Jeremy Payne include a neat sample app showing how Muse Gadgets can stream video from your phone camera, the lack of a remote shutter button made it not so useful for taking photos.
But a few sessions of Claude Code filled in almost all those holes. All I had to do was plug the Waveshare back into my PC, then ask Claude to reprogram each thing I wanted.
When I complained to Claude that I couldn’t properly read or hear Muse’s replies to my asks, issues that others have mentioned as well , Claude built a conversation history page so I can swipe right to read what it said, and I plugged in a British AI voice from ElevenLabs that speaks its answers out loud. (The voice was the least soul-sucking of the ones in ElevenLabs’ free tier, my wife and I agree, even if it doesn’t match the Muse avatars’ cuddly vibe at all.)
Thanks to Claude, I can now press a button to make my phone take a picture from across the room with a high-quality live preview, and my phone’s front-facing camera no longer displays upside down. Claude made fairly short work of adding a low-quality camera preview over Bluetooth, too, so I don’t need to be on home Wi-Fi to get photos from creative angles.
I asked Claude to make a whole batch of different avatars like the ones Meta showed off during Meta Connect, and to add a Tamagotchi-like minigame where they need food, play, sleep, and a bath. When the game seemed too simple to capture any attention, I had it add four different levels of hunger, boredom, and dirt. I decided treats should make a crunchy mess and get avatars dirtier when they eat them, and that too much play should tire out a pet. My wish was Claude’s command.
When I noticed I was accidentally letting go of the push-to-talk button too soon and making Muse choke on almost-empty audio, vibe coding fixed it minutes later by sending only audio over one second in length. The only obvious lag I’m seeing now is from Meta’s own servers — sometimes they’re responsive, sometimes they lag quite a bit.
It was so easy to let Claude reprogram the pendant that I asked it to build a few features specifically for this video in this story, including a working pocket watch face with three hands that actually tells the time. (That took it 15 minutes; now, when I say the hardware looks like a pocket watch, you can see what I mean!) It even found, downloaded, trimmed, and loaded video clips of Zuck introducing the Muse Charm and installed a video player so I could play those clips on the Waveshare.
I want you to understand I have no coding experience, and so I have no idea if any of this code is good. It might be fatally flawed. Nor do I trust Meta or its Muse agent with my email or my home network, particularly after hearing how it leaked one reviewer’s home address . (I put it on guest Wi-Fi from the get-go as a precaution.)
That means I don’t really know how useful a Muse Charm may or may not be for those who do know how to code and are willing to take a bigger leap of faith. But after nearly dropping a bulky little silver pendant a couple of times, one with no more Muse functionality than my phone (and quite a bit less without additional code), I’m thinking Muse itself isn’t the reason to buy a dedicated compute pocket watch.
The reason to have a dedicated piece of hardware is to do things you can’t do on the phone that’s already in your pocket, like coding the entire gadget to do whatever you want. Which makes me wonder: Will the actual Muse Charm be this freely programmable, or would the kind of people who’d buy one be better off with a development kit? I guess we’ll see when it ships.

articles.title_orig: Google says Gemini 4 Argon is the best coder alive, so I put it up against Claude Opus 5.5
articles.title_zh: Google says Gemini 4 Argon is the best coder alive, so I put it up against Claude Opus 5.5
articles.content_orig:
There's a bit of a pattern I've noticed with the major AI labs and the LLMs they launch. One model will be excellent at practically anything you throw at it, while the next one can be an absolute letdown. I've seen this happen with models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and even open-weight offerings from the likes of DeepSeek and Alibaba's Qwen.
There's one company that's been a pretty consistent disappointment, particularly when it comes to coding, though: Google. I'll explain more below, but on September 30, Google announced its latest frontier model: Gemini 4 Argon. The company made some pretty bold claims about its coding capabilities, positioning it as one of the best models for complex software engineering tasks.
Given Gemini's history of letting me down in precisely that department, I was skeptical, to say the least. Still, in the interest of giving it a fair shot, I decided to put Gemini 4 Argon up against Claude Opus 5.5 .
I've been one of the biggest advocates of Google's AI efforts. NotebookLM, for example, is still the AI tool I use most, and I could ramble on about Google's other AI experiments for hours . When it comes to coding, though, Gemini and I have a rather complicated relationship.
I've put Gemini's models up against Claude and ChatGPT multiple times for all sorts of coding tasks. This includes building Chrome extensions , recreating apps from screenshots , developing portfolio websites, and even building my dream note-taking app from scratch. While the results have varied, there's one pattern I've noticed across almost every experiment: Gemini always seems to be in a hurry to finish the job.
It rarely goes beyond the bare minimum, often leaves features unfinished, and sometimes calls a project complete before even checking whether it runs properly. In one experiment, Antigravity built a portfolio website containing just seven of my 400-plus published articles, despite being explicitly asked to include them all. In another, it handed me a note-taking app with several requested features missing and an error that prevented it from launching properly.
This isn't exclusive to one Gemini model, either! I've noticed similar shortcomings across different generations, even with higher reasoning settings enabled. Claude and ChatGPT have certainly disappointed me too, but their weaknesses tend to vary from experiment to experiment. Gemini, meanwhile, has repeatedly fallen short on both the technical implementation and the frontend experience.
I decided to put Argon to the test using an experiment I'd carried out recently, where Gemini had let me down massively. I headed to both Claude Code and Antigravity and instructed them to build me my dream note-taking app.
Whenever I do these experiments, I make it a point to keep my prompts deliberately vague rather than spelling out every single feature I'd like to see. I've found that most AI coding tools are already pretty good at following a detailed set of instructions. What I'm more interested in is seeing how well they can fill in the gaps themselves.
Given that Gemini's biggest weakness in my previous experiments has been doing little more than the bare minimum, I figured this would be the perfect way to see whether Argon was any different. I used Opus 5.5 for Claude Code on the default Medium effort setting, and Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity on Medium effort as well. After tweaking the settings of each tool a bit to ensure both could work without constantly asking me to approve commands or file changes, I let them get to work.
Right off the bat, I noticed Gemini 4 Argon taking its sweet time. It did end up completing the initial build around 20 minutes before Claude Code, but it wasn't rushing through the process. It began by checking the development environment, figuring out what technologies to use, and making decisions about how the app should be structured.
The way it interpreted my prompt caught my attention, too! I'd mentioned being a computer science student and a tech journalist, and instead of treating those details as background information, Argon seemed to build the entire app around them. It decided to create a local-first knowledge workbench with features specifically designed for research, writing, studying, and coding.
Interestingly, it didn't stop there. It came up with an infinite canvas for brainstorming, an Obsidian-like knowledge graph for connecting notes , executable code blocks for programming, spaced-repetition flashcards for studying, and even a fact-checking ledger for keeping track of claims and sources in my articles. It also included a Markdown editor with multiple viewing modes, PDF support with citation linking, and a local vault for storing notes as Markdown files.
None of these were features I'd asked for, and this was a massive step up from previous Gemini models that wouldn't even fully create what I'd explicitly asked for!
Now, everything I've discussed above was based on what Argon had told me in Antigravity. I hadn't actually used the app yet, and for all I knew, it could've been a complete disaster. It had spun up a local server with the app running, and it was finally time to see what it had built.
I've been let down far too many times by Gemini's frontend skills, so I was bracing myself for more of the same. My immediate reaction this time, though, was "wow." Yes, the interface was fairly cluttered, and there was a lot going on, but that was largely because Argon had populated the app with a ton of sample data to demonstrate its features.
Beyond that, the overall design felt surprisingly cohesive. The warm color palette, typography, and layout all worked well together, and for once, it didn't look like another generic vibe-coded app with a dark background and purple gradients.
More importantly, it actually felt like an app designed around my needs rather than a bunch of unrelated features thrown together. The writing interface had its own fact-checking ledger, the spatial canvas let me visually connect research and ideas, and there was a dedicated flashcard system for studying.
I could actually see myself using several of these features regularly.
Argon had created a dedicated Markdown vault where every note was automatically saved as an individual .md file. So, all the data was stored locally on my Mac. I particularly liked this because it meant my notes weren't locked into the app, and I could access them directly from my file system if I wanted to.
There were a couple of hiccups, though. Initially, the local vault wasn't loading properly, and I was greeted with a "Cannot GET /" error when I tried accessing it. So, I headed back to Antigravity, explained what was happening, and Argon got to work fixing it. It updated the server configuration, added a proper vault explorer, and got everything running.
Then, I ran into another issue where the main interface kept refreshing every few seconds. Again, I went back to Antigravity, and Argon figured out that the app's automatic file syncing was triggering a continuous refresh loop. It made a few changes to how the development server watched files and how notes were synced, and that resolved the issue too.
Unlike some of my previous experiences with Gemini, where I'd spend several rounds going back and forth only to end up with another broken implementation, this time it actually seemed to understand the problem and how to solve it! So, Argon 4 defintiely seems like a massive step-up on all accounts.
Now, Claude Code took a completely different approach to the exact same prompt. Claude's version was much closer to what you'd expect from a conventional note-taking app. It had a clean, minimal three-column interface, notebooks, nested tags, daily notes, tasks, a rich-text editor with slash commands, and PDF support. The design was polished, and I'd even argue that it was easier to navigate than Gemini's version at first glance.

articles.title_orig: Chipotle is leaning on new menu items to bring diners back
articles.title_zh: Chipotle is leaning on new menu items to bring diners back
articles.content_orig:
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
Shares of Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) rose 8.9% on Thursday, October 29, 2026, while the S&P 500 fell 0.3%. The gain came a day after Chipotle reported its third-quarter results on October 28. Revenue came in above estimates, while adjusted earnings per share fell below them. Four of the chain’s five peers also posted smaller gains during that session. What in Chipotle’s results did news reports link to the rise?
Chipotle Topped Sales Estimates As Transactions Rose
Chipotle’s third-quarter revenue reached $3,293 million, a little above the $3,287 million analysts expected. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.27, below the $0.29 estimate. The company released its results after the market closed on Wednesday. News reports linked Thursday’s rise to same-store sales that topped estimates, as well as to the chain’s push to bring customer traffic back .
During the October 28 call, management said same-store sales increased 2.1% in the quarter and transactions rose 0.8%. It added that Pollo Asado’s return on August 31 brought in extra transactions, while Chili Lime Chips, launched the same day, got more guests to add chips.
Fresh products give buyers a reason to return; an unchanged lineup can stall. Consider Tesla, which got 98% of last quarter’s deliveries from the Model 3 and Model Y and saw deliveries fall two years in a row. Read Trefis Big Story : How Tesla Blundered .
The industry saw a pullback in the first part of October, management said, but Chipotle’s transactions have since turned positive again. Management expects fourth-quarter same-store sales to rise around 2% overall, with the growth rate reaching 3% to 4% by the end of the quarter as smoked brisket returns to the menu in November.
Margins slipped in the quarter. Management put the company’s restaurant-level margin, its own adjusted measure, at 23.3%. That figure is down 120 basis points from a year earlier.
Did Chipotle Rise With Its Restaurant Peers?
Most of Chipotle’s peers also rose, though by much less. Four of the five companies on the Trefis peer list gained during the session, leaving Restaurant Brands International as the only decline. Texas Roadhouse posted the largest advance among them at 4.7%. The consumer discretionary sector fund, XLY, rose 0.8% on a day the S&P 500 fell. Chipotle rose almost twice as much as Texas Roadhouse, so a large part of its gain was its own rather than the group’s.
Where Does Chipotle Stock Stand After The Jump?
A rise this large is rare for Chipotle. One session in the prior 365 days saw a rise at least as big. After the jump, the stock was still down 22.3% over the twelve months to October 29, compared with a 13.3% gain for the S&P 500.
Much of that fall occurred in the last three months. The shares lost 16.0% from July 31 to October 29, while the S&P 500 rose 3.3%. Chipotle closed the session at $31.28. That price sits above the stock’s 52-week closing low of $27.52 set on October 23, 2026, and remains well below the closing high of $40.87 reached on January 23, 2026.
Chipotle is expected to report its fourth-quarter 2026 results in February 2027. Same-store sales growth is the figure to watch in that report.

articles.title_orig: How Donald Trump And Bill Clinton's Rally Sizes Compare Days Before Midterms
articles.title_zh: How Donald Trump And Bill Clinton's Rally Sizes Compare Days Before Midterms
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump and former President Bill Clinton held rival rallies on Friday in Florida and Mississippi respectively, as both parties deploy their big hitters just four days before the midterm elections.
Trump addressed a rally at the Ocean Center in Daytona Beach while Clinton spoke in Tupelo at the Link Center in support of longshot Mississippi Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom.
The events come as both Republicans and Democrats are trying to mobilize their voters ahead of Tuesday’s elections . Democrats are hoping to flip both chambers of Congress in a move that would dramatically impede Trump’s freedom of action during the final two years of his second term.
Trump has focused heavily on the attendance at his rivals events in recent weeks, and raised the subject again on Friday.
Newsweek contacted President Trump, via the White House by email outside of regular office hours.
A Clinton spokesperson said, "President Clinton was making the case for Scott Colom. Trump was making excuses for senseless wars and nonsensical tariffs that leave Americans paying more for gas and groceries. President Clinton was on offense. Trump was on defense. That’s the story."
According to The Daytona Beach News-Journal Trump’s rally in the city was attended by “a capacity crowd of more than 9,000.” Photographs published by the outlet show packed stands as the president delivered his address.
The Ocean Center in Daytona has a capacity of 9,300 according to its official website , with “more than 200,000 square feet of flexible indoor and outdoor meeting space.”
On X the conservative Right Side Broadcasting Network shared a one-minute video showing packed seating on four sides surrounding the podium at the Daytona rally. They commented : “THE MAINSTREAM MEDIA WON’T SHOW YOU THIS!
“ABSOLUTELY PACKED arena in Daytona Beach, Florida, as THOUSANDS of American patriots turn out for President Trump! The energy is UNREAL!”
Trump supporter Benny Johnson also shared footage from the rally commenting : “The media keeps saying ‘MAGA is dead’… I’m at the Trump rally right now in Daytona Beach and it’s PACKED to the rafters.”
Conservative commentator Eric Daugherty posted footage of Trump being applauded as he arrived to make his speech and said there were “THOUSANDS OF PEOPLE” still waiting outside the venue at this point. This has not been independently confirmed by Newsweek .
Clinton’s rally in Tupelo was attended by “roughly 400 people” according to Mississippi Today . Local outlet WTVA reported the venue, the Link Center, had a capacity of “approximately 400” as well as “additional overflow space available for 100 people.” It is unclear whether the overflow space was used for the rally.
WTVA reporter Ross Adams shared a video from the rally on X showing Clinton addressing a cheering crowd on a theatre like stage. He added: “The man famous for shaking every hand in the room could be here all night as @BillClinton makes his way to a crowd in Tupelo, following a wide ranging speech criticizing the Trump administration and boosting @scott_colom’s long shot bid for an historic upset in just days.”
Photographs from the event taken by a Getty photographer showed Clinton speaking in front of a large Mississippi flag, flanked with American flags, while one supporter held up a placard reading “MISSISSIPPI FORWARD.”
During Trump’s rally the president accused the media of downplaying attendance at his rallies commenting : “They never like mentioning crowd side because crowd size means success and they, the fake news, do not want us to succeed.”
Trump said Tuesday’s polls will be “the most important midterm elections ever” and said he was campaigning to “stop America-hating communists from taking over the United States Congress.”
Meanwhile, Clinton advocated for Mississippi Democratic Senate candidate Colom commenting : “I’m supporting Scott because he will honestly give you his opinion, and if you disagree, he’ll have a conversation with you. And if you can change his mind, he’ll change his mind.
“You can’t put MAGA first. You have to put Mississippi first.”
Colom also gave an address in which he focused on the cost of living. The Democratic candidate said: “They were promised lower grocery prices. That’s what I’m going to fight for.
“That’s my message to them. I’m going to give you what you were promised in 2024. You were promised no more endless wars. I’m going to give you no more endless wars.”
A number of politicians have made reference to the size of their rallies, or those of their opponents, ahead of the midterm elections.
On Thursday Texas Democratic Senate hopeful James Talarico told CNN his Republican rival Ken Paxton was “canceling rallies because nobody is showing up.”
The comment came after Paxton’s team cancelled a scheduled rally on November 1 in El Paso citing scheduling and logistics.
During a rally in Perry, Georgia, on Oct. 24 Trump took aim at the crowd size attracted by former President Barack Obama during a rally in Michigan.
He said: “You know I saw Barack Hussein Obama was in Michigan and the place was empty. And they were saying, ‘Oh this is a large crowd coming the people are tricking through.’ They don’t talk about my crowds, they never talk about them.”
Trump has a record of including Obama’s middle name when mentioning the former president, in what critics argue is an attempt to make him sound more Islamic.
Obama’s Michigan rally was held at the Cass Technical High School which has a 3,000 person capacity gym, with room for around 4,300, including overflow areas, for major events such as political rallies. Photographs from the event showed a good attendance and one commentator reported there was an overflow crowd.

articles.title_orig: Opposition bloc said weighing direct PM elections to break political deadlock
articles.title_zh: Opposition bloc said weighing direct PM elections to break political deadlock
articles.content_orig:
Israel faces weeks, possibly months, of political limbo after final results show there’s no clear winner in its elections .
Neither of the two main blocs – one led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud party, the other led by the centrist Yashar party of his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot – have reached the required 61-seat majority to form a government in Israel’s 120-seat parliament.
So how could a new government be formed?
Certainly, it does not look easy, with deep-rooted political and ideological divisions making any seemingly straightforward coalition almost impossible.
Still, it can be done, even if the result is a tenuous alliance that survives little more than a year or so in office. If party leaders are unable to figure it out in the 12 weeks they will have available, then Israelis will be back at the polls.
Here’s some potential scenarios that could avoid that.
On paper, the opposition’s surest path to unseat Netanyahu is built on Jewish-Arab cooperation. And that is its biggest obstacle.
Two of the opposition bloc’s right-wing party leaders, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and former Defense Minister Avigdor Liberman, oppose any government that depends on the two Arab parties in parliament – the Joint List and Raam – whether it’s from inside the coalition, or as outside supporters of a minority government. The two leaders have hardened their positions since the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023.
Only one government in Israel’s history has enjoyed the full participation of an Arab party. Raam was part of an eight-party coalition that succeeded in ousting Netanyahu in 2021, but it collapsed just after a year in office.
Even without forming a government, the opposition parties could still work together and leverage their parliamentary majority to replace the Knesset speaker, along with other key positions, and thereby constrain Netanyahu’s caretaker government as it continued in power. But the prospects of assembling a coalition to replace him as Israel’s leader remain highly complicated and politically charged.
Another option would see the implosion of the two blocs in favor of a unity government. Netanyahu’s Likud party would certainly be involved, along with some of his existing coalition partners, as well as – crucially – at least one party from the opposition bloc.
Netanyahu, in this case, is believed to be willing to part ways with his far-right National Security Minister Ben-Gvir – but not from far-right Finance Minister Bezazel Smotrich and the ultra-Orthodox parties.
Eisenkot , however, has ruled out sitting with Netanyahu, and it would be seen by many Israelis desperate to see the back of ‘Bibi’ as an act of betrayal if he were to change his mind.
Another scenario could see Netanyahu encouraging defections from opposition parties or individual lawmakers.
But all four opposition bloc party leaders – Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman and Yair Golan – have declared they will not sit with him. And with Netanyahu’s bloc a full eight seats short, persuading eight individual defectors sets a high bar.
While all these possibilities are being discussed in the background, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will hold a very public round of consultations with the leaders of the parties that have made it into parliament.
Once he has solicited their opinions, he will task one of those leaders with the job of trying to form a government. Arab parties are expected to voice their support for Eisenkot, so the Yashar leader could be asked to go first.
Whoever gets the nod will have 28 days to complete the job, with a possible 14-day extension if needed.
If it all comes to nothing, the president will ask a second leader to have a go. They get 28 days only to sort it out.
After that, a majority of Knesset members could ask the president to task a third candidate, who then has 14 days to build a coalition.
If none of these produce a breakthrough, there will be another election.
The person who appears best-placed to navigate this timetable is Netanyahu. As caretaker prime minister, he can afford to wait: If main rival Eisenkot gets the first shot – and fails – the mandate is likely to pass to him. And if he fails as well, the political deadlock seems certain to lead Israel to another round of elections – with Netanyahu remaining caretaker for months, until another government is formed.
A repeat election – which would happen no earlier than next spring – is a real possibility, as these results look set to return Israel to a state of political paralysis and what would be the seventh general election in eight years.

articles.title_orig: 'A lot of lies': Kaja Kallas criticises Russian FM Lavrov following G20 meetings
articles.title_zh: 'A lot of lies': Kaja Kallas criticises Russian FM Lavrov following G20 meetings
articles.content_orig:
European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov of telling "a lot of lies" on topics such as the Ukraine war during talks with G20 ministers in Atlanta on Friday.
"We were talking about the big geopolitical crisis, including Ukraine, and we were able to address Sergey Lavrov head on with this," she told the AFP news agency.
"Of course, he put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives" that Europeans challenged, Kallas added.
European officials also reportedly used the opportunity to put further pressure on Moscow as they sought to secure a ceasefire in the Black Sea - prompting pushback from Lavrov, a diplomatic source told AFP.
British Foreign Minister Ed Miliband said he had also told Lavrov in the plenary that "he should have the courage to tell Putin that Russia will not win this war."
The UK minister is also said to have confronted Lavrov over a recent attack on a Dnipro railway that killed 15 people as he stressed Moscow was the "aggressor" in the conflict, which began in February 2022 when Russian forces launched their full-scale invasion.
In a press conference on Friday, Lavrov "welcomed" the US' willingness to engage in dialogue with Moscow while hitting out at what he called Europe's "arrogant boycott."
"This is a good lesson for our European colleagues," he said of Washington's approach.
Several officials at the meetings also reportedly refused to stand for a "family photo" with Lavrov, leading US organisers to cancel the picture.
The G20 meetings come just days before the US' key midterm elections, which will determine the balance of power in Congress for President Donald Trump's final two years in office.
On Friday, the US State Department announced that Washington had green-lit a package of 500 Patriot PAC-3 interceptors worth $2.1 billion for Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has continued to plead with US and European allies for more interceptors for its forces as Ukraine continues to weather Russian missile and drone attacks.
And while he welcomed the new package and thanked the US for its "strong decision," he warned that delivery could take years.
"Five hundred PAC-3 interceptors is a substantial number, and very soon – this winter – they COULD make for a highly effective defence package," Zelenskyy wrote in a post on X.
"However, it has been stipulated that deliveries may begin ONLY IN A FEW YEARS," he added. "We are asking our American partners to find a solution for the time when there is a real danger and a real need to use PAC-3 interceptors."
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Lavrov on the sidelines of the G20 in Atlanta.

articles.title_orig: Report from the Vatican
articles.title_zh: Report from the Vatican
articles.content_orig:
Speaking to the participants of the meeting, âThe Future of AI: A Dialogue Between the Vatican and the Scientific World on the Developments and Applications of Intelligent Technologiesâ, Pope Leo XIV pointed out that coming from different countries brings new questions and perspectives.
Nevertheless, âyou share a certain sense of unease regarding the development of artificial intelligence. We recognize the direction we should take, yet not enough is being done to move forward,â he argued.
The groupâs concerns, ideas, and suggestions for the future are the âfirst fruits of a transdisciplinary approachâ, which is more and more needed in order to address the complex challenges of the day.
The Pope highlighted that the Pontifical Academy for Life and the Future of Life Institute, who jointly organized this meeting, are âwell aware of the challenges that arise wherever human dignity is threatened.â
With this in mind, he recalled Pope Francisâ words to the G7 leaders in 2024 , where he described AI âan exciting and fearsome toolâ and stressed that no machine should ever be able to choose whether to take human life.
These words still ring true, the Pope said. Turning to his own encyclical Magnifica Humanitas , Pope Leo outlined five considerations regarding artificial intelligence: the future of AI is not pre-determined; machines are tools, not people; certain decisions cannot ever be delegated; intelligent technologies must be directed to the common good; and institutions are needed to put ethical principles into practice to guide AI development.
The future of artificial intelligence is not pre-determined. Since human beings develop AI, its future relies on the choices humanity makes. That is why, the Pope stressed, âwe have the responsibility to guide, change, and, when necessary, reject its applications.â
Therefore, the question is not just, âWhat can AI do?â Instead, it needs to be, âWhat purpose should it serve?â
Developing AI should not mean focusing solely on the finish line and ignoring those left behind. Pope Leo argued that a reliable system that serves the human person has much greater value than one that is powerful but whose âconsequences cannot be adequately foreseen or controlled.â
The second consideration the Pope explained is that machines are tools and not persons. They do not have experiences, bodies, feelings, relationships, and do not understand love, work, or responsibility.
Some have suggested giving these systems rights or legal personhood. However, Pope Leo underlined how this risks âobscuring human responsibility and leaving those who suffer harm to confront a faceless entity.â
Thirdly, there are certain decisions that should never be given to machines. For example, putting a person on a target list or in a border control database means they will become simply a data point.
âDecisions affecting human life, freedom and the use of force must always remain subject to effective, informed, and responsible human oversight,â the Pope explained. That is why AI must be âdisarmedâ. Furthermore, he encouraged the States meeting in Geneva in November to take steps to ban lethal autonomous weapons.
The fourth consideration is that intelligent technologies should be geared towards the common good. âIndeed, they must never become ends in themselves or serve merely the interests of a privileged few,â the Pope stressed to the participants.
These technologies should encourage solidarity and participation at different levels of the global community, making sure the benefits of progress are enjoyed equally.
Pope Leoâs final consideration is a challenge, which he described as potentially the most urgent. The world needs institutions capable of putting ethical principles into practice to guide AI into practice and a focus on protecting the common good.
What this calls for is âshared standards, independent oversight, and clear mechanisms of accountability, so that decisions concerning the development and use of AI can be examined, challenged when necessary, and accompanied by appropriate remedies for any harm caused.â
Pope Leo closed his address to the meeting participants expressing his gratitude for their contributions in the field of AI and encouraging them to persevere, and work together with a spirit of dialogue and shared responsibility directed to the common good.
âI accompany you with my prayers, and to each of you I cordially impart my blessing.â

articles.title_orig: California housing market remains brutal nightmare for buyers — it gets worse for ordinary families
articles.title_zh: California housing market remains brutal nightmare for buyers — it gets worse for ordinary families
articles.content_orig:
California’s housing market remains a brutal nightmare for buyers, with ordinary families needing a staggering $228,000 annual income just to afford a typical home.
A measly 19% of households could afford a median-priced, existing single-family home in the Golden State during the third quarter, according to figures released Friday by the California Association of Realtors.
The dismal affordability rate was unchanged from the previous quarter and the same period last year, offering little relief to Californians hoping to buy a piece of the American Dream .
The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.
Even as home prices dipped, higher mortgage rates kept the cost of buying painfully high, leaving would-be homeowners facing enormous monthly payments.
The minimum qualifying household income needed to purchase a median-priced California home hit $228,000 in the third quarter, unchanged from the previous quarter and $4,400 higher than a year earlier.
Buyers also faced a monthly mortgage bill of $5,700, including principal, interest, taxes and insurance. That figure was flat from the second quarter but up 2% year over year.

California’s monthly housing payment remained more than twice the national average of $2,760, according to C.A.R.
And the affordability crunch shows little sign of easing. The income required to buy a typical California home has topped $200,000 in 15 of the past 16 quarters.
Mortgage rates could remain elevated over the coming months, with inflation likely to stay high in the near term, further squeezing the purchasing power of prospective buyers, the association warned.
The numbers were especially punishing across Southern California, where home prices and the salaries needed to keep up varied sharply by county.
In the Los Angeles metro area, an existing single-family home carried a median price tag of $847,030 in the third quarter, requiring a monthly mortgage payment of $5,390 and a minimum qualifying household income of $215,600.
The price was even steeper in Los Angeles County, where homes cost a median $958,450. Buyers needed to earn at least $244,000 annually to handle monthly payments of $6,100.
Orange County was in another league entirely, with a typical single-family home costing $1.47 million.
Prospective buyers there needed a jaw-dropping $374,400 in annual household income to qualify, with monthly mortgage payments reaching $9,360.

articles.title_orig: Finland’s Stubb Rebuts Report on Putin Slavic History Lecture
articles.title_zh: Finland’s Stubb Rebuts Report on Putin Slavic History Lecture
articles.content_orig:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.
"We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," Støre said.
Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.
The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and Støre debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the 90-minute call - held from Helsinki - to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
Putin also reaffirmed to the Nordic leaders what he views as the "root causes" of the conflict - his frequent shorthand for Ukraine's desire to exist as a sovereign state.
"A fair long-term peace settlement is possible only if Russia's legal interests are taken into account fully and unconditionally", Putin said.
All three parties reportedly agreed to continue their direct phone communication.
There was no official EU reaction to the talks. The dialogue had not been coordinated with other European leaders, the Danish and Swedish prime ministers said. "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo," commented Sweden's Ulf Kristersson.
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US and Ukraine and its European allies have soured since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia, allowing Moscow to export oil to the America.
As the Trump administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to re-establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
Soon after, Putin visited Alaska for a summit with Trump, and from then on Europeans were further sidelined from Ukraine peace talks. Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the EU of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".
And although he said Moscow did not view Finland and Norway as speaking on behalf of Europe, on Tuesday Peskov conceded that Stubb and Støre's talks with Putin had been "very constructive and practical talks with the leaders of two key neighbouring states."

articles.title_orig: Ethiopian PM Abiy Ahmed puts ministers through military training
articles.title_zh: Ethiopian PM Abiy Ahmed puts ministers through military training
articles.content_orig:
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has put his cabinet ministers and other senior government officials through military training, saying armed forces discipline can help build stronger leaders and advance the country's development.
Photos shared by him on social media show him taking part in military exercises alongside ministers, deputy ministers and heads of government institutions at the Hurso military training centre.
The move is unusual in Ethiopia, where senior civilian government officials are rarely seen undergoing military training.
Those taking part include Speaker of the House of Federation Muferiat Kamil, Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa and Health Minister Mekdes Daba.
It is unclear when the training began or how long it is expected to last.
In his post, the prime minister, who is known as Abiy, said Ethiopia's ambition to achieve universal prosperity required its leadership to be physically fit, morally strong and intellectually capable.
He said military institutions offered valuable lessons in discipline, patriotism, teamwork, accountability and leadership.
"Soldiers have targets while civilians have goals. The objective of both is victory," he said, adding that combining military and civilian disciplines would help create a generation capable of achieving both.
Abiy argued that military training could help develop leaders with a strong sense of purpose, responsibility and the ability to work together towards common objectives.
The training comes as Ethiopia faces multiple security challenges, including continued fighting in parts of the northern Tigray region, conflict in Amhara and insecurity in Oromia.
It also takes place amid heightened tensions with neighbouring Eritrea, with concerns over the possibility of renewed conflict between the two countries.
Abiy has previously emphasised military preparedness and national development as central to his government's ambitions.

articles.title_orig: The cursed cruise: how the dream of never-ending luxury at sea became a nightmare
articles.title_zh: The cursed cruise: how the dream of never-ending luxury at sea became a nightmare
articles.content_orig:
A cruise promising passengers a lifetime at sea came to an abrupt halt in Cambodia after soaring fuel costs made the voyage too expensive to continue. Passengers who had spent months living aboard the Villa Vie Odyssey said they were given just seven hours' notice to leave the ship.
The captain of the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship is speaking out after 203 residents were forced to disembark in Cambodia due to a critical fuel shortage, calling the ordeal "really painful."
The ship, which offered passengers the chance to make the ocean their permanent home, suspended its around-the-world voyage earlier this week after soaring fuel costs made continued operations financially unsustainable, according to its operator.
Residents were forced to leave the vessel in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville, just two years after the ship set sail from Belfast, Northern Ireland , on what was supposed to be a 3 1/2-year journey around the world.
THOUSANDS BOOKED TROPICAL BAHAMAS CRUISE AND ENDED UP IN FREEZING CANADA INSTEAD
"I feel awful. They’re counting on me to make the decisions here, and there’s nothing else I’m focused on. I’m the villain in the story, but I’m doing everything I can to support the residents [with] a solution," Mikael Petterson, founder and executive chairman of Villa Vie Residences, told Business Insider.
Some residents had paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the chance to live aboard.
The Villa Vie Odyssey had marketed its around-the-world journey as an alternative to traditional retirement, offering residents the opportunity to live permanently at sea. (AFP via Getty Images)
Villa Vie Residences had offered lifetime access to the ship through its "Endless Horizons" program for a one-time payment of $299,999 for a single-occupancy cabin or $499,999 for double occupancy, Fox Business reported in May 2024.
Captain Emanuele Giudice on Thursday opened up about what led to the decision to force residents off the ship.
"Unfortunately, due to the shortage of fuel, we needed to shut down one generator, chiller, non-essential lights," Giudice said, as Reuters reported.
CRUISE PASSENGERS FACE BLOCKED ACCESS AS ANGRY PROTESTERS SET BARRICADES ON FIRE
Giudice said the shutdowns would have "created discomfort to the residents, which — we don't want that."
"So we kindly asked the residents to get off the ship because our fuel situation was critical," he said.
"There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do."
Asked who was to blame, Giudice pointed to high fuel prices, saying they had significantly affected the ship's travel.
CRUISE FEE DOUBLES AT VACATION HOT SPOT AS PASSENGERS BRACE FOR EVEN STEEPER HIKES
He declined to comment when a reporter asked whether the war in the Middle East and President Donald Trump were responsible.
Giudice also said residents were given more than 24 hours' notice to leave the ship. Yet passengers previously told The Associated Press (AP) they received just seven hours' notice and had to make their own accommodations .
The cruise ship suspended its around-the-world voyage after soaring fuel costs left its operator unable to financially sustain continued operations. (Tang Chhin Sothy/AFP via Getty Images)
Paul and Lynn Montoya, a retired couple from Wyoming, previously told AP they were repeatedly asked for fuel money.
"I’m the villain in the story, but I’m doing everything I can to support the residents on a solution."
"We were tired of every two to four weeks being asked for money for fuel, money for everything," Lynn Montoya said.

"We had hopes, but they just kept sinking further and further into the hole," she added.
Benjamin Schatz, a retiree who had hoped to make the MV Odyssey his forever home, told CBS News he was devastated after being forced to leave the ship.
Villa Vie Odyssey Capt. Emanuele Giudice, seen at center, said a critical fuel shortage forced the crew to shut down certain systems aboard the ship. (Tang Chhin Sothy/AFP via Getty Images)
"Honestly, right now, I'm in denial and in shock, and I'm heartbroken," Schatz said, as CBS reported.
He added, "There are people now who are homeless and who have very little money and don't know what they're going to do."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS
The company had marketed life aboard the Odyssey as an alternative to traditional retirement, appealing to retirees concerned about inflation, rising living expenses and the possibility of outliving their savings.
Petterson promoted the experience as a way for retirees to live on a fixed budget without worrying about ongoing expenses.

"For less than the price of an average home, you can secure a lifetime of experiences," Petterson said at the time.
Residents of the Villa Vie Odyssey seen above were forced to leave the cruise ship in Cambodia after its operator said continued operations were financially unsustainable. (Tang Chhin Sothy/AFP via Getty Images)

articles.content_orig:
Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever
Featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance, faster wireless connectivity, and water and dust resistance
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today unveiled the all-new iPad mini , featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. 1 The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. 2 A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support. 3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever.
The new iPad mini is powered by iPadOS 27 with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions on virtually any topic with broad world knowledge, and understand what’s on their screen. 4 The combination of powerful features and game-changing iPadOS 27 capabilities makes the new iPad mini a compelling value. Customers can pre-order it along with the new Smart Folio starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.
“iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.”
Thinner and Lighter Than Ever
At 5.4 mm thin, the new iPad mini is more portable than ever, and is available in two gorgeous finishes: a new midnight and a beautiful starlight. Remarkably thinner and lighter than the previous generation, iPad mini is now even easier to carry, whether a user is reading, working on the go, or using it with one hand. It also features an IP67 rating to protect against water and dust — ideal for a range of use cases, such as working outside on a rainy day or reading by the pool. 1
The new iPad mini comes with a stunning OLED display that delivers amazing front-of-screen performance and an even larger 8.5-inch size while maintaining the same footprint as the previous mini, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. 2 The Super Retina XDR display features OLED technology to deliver pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vivid and accurate imagery.
For an even better visual experience across a range of lighting conditions, iPad mini also features peak brightness of up to 1200 nits — more than 2x higher than the previous generation — and supports 600 nits of full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content, along with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. And with a 1-nit minimum brightness, iPad mini is even more suitable for dim environments, from users reading in bed at night to pilots checking their electronic flight bag in the cockpit. iPad mini also offers a new nano-texture display option, which users love on iPad Pro, that reduces glare in bright environments — ideal for creatives editing outdoors or technicians working in the field. Together, these display advancements extend the versatility of iPad mini across an even wider range of use cases.
A Huge Leap in Performance
A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks. It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. 3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. 3 A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps. 3
The 512GB configuration features a powerful Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which offers double the processing power of the previous generation, accelerating tasks in apps like Draw Things and Detail. By engaging all 32 cores, A20 Pro becomes a powerhouse for more advanced on-device AI workloads. A20 Pro also brings over a 2x increase in unified memory bandwidth, unlocking additional performance for new levels of capability and responsiveness across graphics and AI-intensive workloads.
A Rich New Audio Experience and Advanced Cameras
The new iPad mini features an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs. The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating.
The 12MP Center Stage front camera is now on the landscape edge, perfect for FaceTime calls, video conferencing, and collaboration. And the 12MP Wide back camera captures gorgeous photos with Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, while the addition of an Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and makes document scanning better than ever.
N1 and C2 Come to iPad mini
iPad mini now features N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. 5 N1 brings better performance when connected to 5GHz Wi-Fi networks and improves the overall performance and reliability of features like AirDrop and AirPlay. 6
Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system. C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency. 6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit. Users can also enjoy the benefits of eSIM, which lets them quickly and securely add a new plan, connect and transfer existing plans digitally, and stay in touch with family and friends regardless of Wi-Fi availability. 7
iPadOS 27 with the Next Generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI
iPad mini users can get even more done with Siri AI, rolling out in beta with iPadOS 27. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational. 4 iPad mini also supports Apple’s most advanced on-device model ever, for even more expressive voices with Siri AI as well as a major boost in accuracy with systemwide dictation.

articles.title_orig: Russia’s Warplanes Are Burning, Crashing, and Disappearing—13 Lost in Five Weeks
articles.title_zh: Russia’s Warplanes Are Burning, Crashing, and Disappearing—13 Lost in Five Weeks
articles.content_orig:
This was reported by the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense , according to Ukrinform.
As the agency notes, such losses are quite significant for the aggressor country’s aircraft fleet, as its restoration requires a lengthy production cycle, substantial financial resources, and specialized industrial cooperation. By way of comparison: the number of Su-34s destroyed is equivalent to approximately 2.5–3 years of their production, based on an estimated production capacity of 14–18 aircraft per year.
As of October 22, according to intelligence data, the Russian Federation’s Aerospace Forces had approximately 140 Su-34s of various modifications in service, including the upgraded Su-34M (Su-34NVO).
It is emphasized that the sheer numbers of the Russian Su-34 fleet do not fully reflect its actual combat capability. Such an assessment must take into account a range of factors: the technical condition of the aircraft, the number of trained crews, the intensity of operation, maintenance capabilities, and the ability to replace losses.
According to the Main Intelligence Directorate (GUR), the Su-34s deployed in the war against Ukraine are one of the key components of the enemy’s strike aviation. The use of these aircraft as carriers of guided aerial bombs has enabled the aggressor country to expand its capabilities for striking ground targets, particularly in areas of active combat operations and in settlements near the front lines.
Despite significant combat losses, Russia continues to produce and modernize the Su-34, seeking to maintain the size of its air fleet and sustain the intensity of its missile and bomb strikes. The potential for further expansion of this capability depends on production capacity, the availability of technological components, and the ability of the aggressor country’s military-industrial complex to compensate for losses.
Serial production of the Su-34 is concentrated at the V.P. Chkalov Novosibirsk Aviation Plant, which is part of the United Aircraft Corporation of the Russian Federation. The production capacity of this facility allows for the manufacture of approximately 14–18 aircraft of this type per year.
The priority is the production of modernized Su-34Ms, which feature improved onboard equipment and expanded capabilities for the use of airborne weapons. The modernization is intended to enhance the aircraft’s effectiveness, taking into account combat experience gained during the war against Ukraine.
At the same time, production resources are divided between the needs of the Russian military and export orders. In particular, part of the production capacity is dedicated to fulfilling a contract to supply Su-34ME aircraft to Algeria. This places an additional strain on the production system, forcing Russia to balance replenishing its own air fleet with fulfilling international contractual obligations.
“However, between October 22, 2025, and October 22, 2026, 22 new Su-34s were delivered to the Russian Aerospace Forces. This figure exceeds the estimated annual production volume by 14–18 aircraft,” the Main Intelligence Directorate reports.
Intelligence data indicates that during the initial phase of the full-scale invasion, the Russians used the Su-34 primarily to bomb ground targets with unguided aerial bombs, including the FAB-250, FAB-500 M-62, and the concrete-piercing BetAB-500. The use of such weapons required the aircraft to fly close to their targets, which increased their vulnerability to Ukraine’s air defense systems.
At the same time, the enemy began using the Su-34 as a platform for the Kh-31 and Kh-59 guided air-to-air missiles, as well as, in some cases, the Kh-35U anti-ship missiles to strike ground targets.
As noted by the Main Intelligence Directorate, fundamental changes in Russian aviation tactics occurred with the widespread introduction of aerial bombs equipped with a standardized guidance and correction module. The combination of the Su-34 with relatively inexpensive UMPC kits became one of the key factors in the aggressor country’s buildup of its strike aviation capabilities.
These guidance and correction modules enable Russian invaders to convert significant stockpiles of conventional aerial bombs into guided munitions suitable for use from a distance, thereby reducing risks to the carrier aircraft, as the Su-34s can remain outside the engagement ranges of certain Ukrainian air defense systems.
The use of Su-34s in Russia’s “scorched earth” tactics leads to large-scale destruction of infrastructure, civilian casualties, and the forced displacement of survivors from frontline communities.
According to intelligence data, the Russian aircraft manufacturing industry remains dependent on a complex supply chain for electronic components, high-tech equipment, and specialized materials. Of particular importance are components for avionics, navigation systems, communications equipment, and electronic warfare systems, as well as industrial and measuring equipment necessary for the manufacture of modern aircraft.
International sanctions are hindering Russian manufacturers’ access to certain critically important technologies. Under these conditions, the aggressor country continues to use schemes involving intermediary entities, third countries, and alternative import channels to meet the needs of its military-industrial complex.
“In this regard, intensifying sanctions pressure on Russia remains a pressing issue. Specifically, this involves the ability to block mechanisms for circumventing sanctions, strengthen export controls, and restrict Russian companies’ access to critical production technologies for the Russian aircraft manufacturing industry—technologies that allow Moscow to continue its genocidal war against Ukraine,” the Main Intelligence Directorate states.
As reported by Ukrinform, in October, the Russian army suffered record casualties on the front line s.
